sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a cycle, not a straight line.
Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 to $37.4 billion [F3][D93], with the Wirtgen acquisition adding 12% to net sales that year [P72].
The peak came in FY2023 at $61.3 billion [F8], then revenue fell 15.6% in FY2024 [D367] and 11.7% in FY2025 [D412].
The FY2024 decline reflected lower shipment volumes across equipment segments as rising grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates weighed on demand [P17].
Production Agriculture was the largest driver, at 37.1% of FY2025 revenue [D657], and it fell 17.6% in FY2025, subtracting 7.0pp from growth [D658][D659].
Production & Precision Agriculture volumes fell 30% in the U.S. and Canada, partly offset by a 22% increase in Brazil [P10].
Construction & Forestry was 25.5% of FY2025 revenue [D889] and fell 11.8%, a 3.0pp drag [D890][D891].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 16.9% CAGR to FY2024 against 6.2% for revenue [F159][F157], but incremental operating margin turned negative in FY2024 at 41.1% [D388].
Diluted EPS compounded at 16.1% against net income at 14.2% [F162][F160], helped by the diluted share count falling 1.9% in FY2025 [D427].
Operating margin was 17.5% in FY2024 [F30], above the 12.1% window median [D1335] but below the 21.2% FY2023 high [F29][D1334].
Net margin fell 2.7pp to 11.0% in FY2025 [F50][D422], still above the 9.6% window median [D1338].
Small Agriculture & Turf operating profit fell on lower sales volumes and mix and higher tariffs, partly offset by price realization [P8].
SG&A was 10.2% of revenue in FY2025 versus 7.5% in FY2023 [D394][D304], and R&D was 5.1% versus a 4.5% median [D393][D1344].
The effective tax rate was 20.1% in FY2025 [D400], so net margin tracked operating margin rather than diverging on tax.
Operating cash flow was $7.46 billion and free cash flow $6.10 billion in FY2025 [F80][F100], a 13.4% FCF margin [D398] against an 11.6% window median [D1341].
FCF was 1.21x net income in FY2025 [D402], above the 0.91x window median [D1347].
Operating inflows were driven by net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in sales receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5].
Capex was $1.36 billion, 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A [F90][D397][D403], so capital intensity stayed modest.
Net debt was $5.52 billion at FY2025 [D407], down from $35.8 billion in FY2021 [D226], or 12.1% of revenue [D408].
That net cash position ranks at the 100th percentile of seven industrials peers, whose median is -38.8% of revenue [D1357][D1358].
Buybacks plus dividends were $2.86 billion, 46.9% of free cash flow [D409][D410], and the diluted share count fell 1.9% [D427].
Return on average equity was 20.6% [D411], below the 28.3% peer median [D1362].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025 [F9][F10][R1], a two-year contraction rather than a single down year.
Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue, fell 17.6% in FY2025 [D657][D658][R2], and Construction & Forestry fell 11.8% [D890][R4].
The allowance for credit losses rose on higher expected losses in agriculture and turf accounts amid elevated delinquencies and weaker market conditions [P4].
FY2017 SG&A was later reported as $3,098.0 million against $3,066.6 million first reported, a data-quality note on that year's cost line [X34][R8].
If FY2026 operating margin falls below the 12.1% window median [D1335], the margin recovery thesis breaks; it will appear in the FY2026 10-K.
If free cash flow margin drops below the 11.6% window median [D1341], cash conversion has weakened; watch the FY2026 cash flow statement.
Management forecasts lower equipment-operations operating cash flow in 2026 on lower net income, partly offset by inventory reductions [P6].
